Article Title: Lack of empathy over terror concerns, trade 'bump': Jaishankar explains what weighs on India-US ties
Article Text:
Jaishankar said the two sides had reached “more or less an understanding” on the trade agreement.

India-US ties

: Trade talks remain a key issue

Jaishankar says India-China ties improving

Ukraine, Iran conflicts pose risks to Global South

'World moving towards greater multipolarity'

NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Tuesday flagged a lack of “understanding or appreciation or empathy” in the US towards India’s concerns over cross-border terrorism, saying the issue has affected bilateral ties.Speaking at the Asia Society in New York after the conclusion of the UN General Assembly’s High-Level Week, Jaishankar said terrorism remains a key concern for India, given its experience of cross-border attacks over several decades.“Terrorism emanating from its neighbour is one of India’s primary concerns, and if this is not fully appreciated by New Delhi's partners, it impacts bilateral ties,” Jaishankar said, in an apparent reference to India-US relations amid closer engagement between Washington and Islamabad.“What for us in India is particularly important is the issue of terrorism... There are very few countries which have been subjected to the kind of terrorism that we have from a neighbor as part of a deliberate, conscious policy over many decades. It is something which matters so deeply to us. There isn't enough understanding or appreciation or empathy of that. I think that creates a problem too,” he said.Jaishankar also discussed the challenges facing India-US relations, including negotiations on a trade agreement.He said the talks were complex because of the fundamental differences between the two economies, including India’s large base of small producers, farmers and factories.“Much of the world has had a more difficult relationship with the US... In our case, one was the trade negotiation. If you look at the stakes involved, the complexity of it involved, bear in mind, India is a society of small producers, small agriculture producers, small factories. Apart from the per capita gap between India and the US, the nature of production and the nature of society are very different. A trade negotiation required a certain amount of patience and detailing to see it through,” he said.Jaishankar said the two sides had reached “more or less an understanding” on the trade agreement, but changes in the US tariff framework had created a new challenge.“We have reached a situation where there is more or less an understanding on the trade agreement. But as my trade minister has said on more than one occasion, the issue is now what has changed on the American side. On the American side, reciprocal tariffs were struck down. So there's now a new basis for tariff imposition, which is 301. And the 301 process is still in the works... that did create bumps last year for the relationship. If that agreement is closed out, that would be one point which would contribute to a better relationship,” he added.He also highlighted the growing influence of public opinion on diplomacy, particularly in democratic countries, saying social media had added a new dimension to international relations.“Today the economics of mobility and the politics of mobility are at odds with each other.... That certainly, in public perception, is an issue... our diplomacy today is not just conducted by states, leaders, ministers, or even by diplomats. In a social media era, there is a very big public opinion factor, which, particularly in democratic societies, makes itself felt. I think that's a reality we have to take into account. .. We would certainly hope for and expect the relationship to move on an upward trajectory. But I have to be real about the issues that we confront. And to the extent we are able to move ahead on some of these issues, I think we'll have a better relationship. Let's apply the lens of...”On India-China relations, Jaishankar said ties were better than they were in 2025 and had improved further compared with 2024, pointing to the easing of the border standoff.“If you asked me, compared to where you were in 2025, is the relationship better today? I would say yes. Compared to 2024, even more so... After what happened in 2020 and the long standoff that we had on the border, the relationship had really been impacted... once the border standoff was resolved, it was natural that this would start to improve,” he said.Jaishankar said India had consistently conveyed to Beijing that a prolonged standoff between the two countries would not benefit either side.“We have long been telling the Chinese, personally at my level, that a standoff between us, a dip in our relationship, doesn't help either of us. Third parties will take advantage of that... It took a little while for the Chinese side to agree with that, for whatever reason. But I don't think that long standoff served our interests. It certainly didn't serve theirs... what we've had is that, as the border comes back more towards normalcy, the relationship comes back more towards normalcy. .. If it happens, it helps both of us,” he said.He said the two countries had arrived at a basic principle that the state of the border determines the broader state of the relationship.“We came down to a very fundamental principle, which is that the state of the border determines the state of the relationship. You can't have tension...on the border and say the relationship should be normal. So what we've had is, as the border comes back more towards normalcy, the relationship comes back more towards normalcy, and if the relationship comes back more towards normalcy, it helps both of us,” Jaishankar said.Jaishankar also highlighted the economic impact of the Ukraine and Iran-Gulf conflicts on developing economies, particularly through energy and food security.“If you look at these two conflicts, the Ukraine and the Iran-Gulf conflict, they've actually had a devastating impact on Global South economies. We are particularly concerned about the energy situation, because the market is very tight. On top of that, if people play politics with it, it adds to the market complications. It will drive up prices at a time when people should be stabilizing prices. A part of it is the security of oil supplies, and another is the politics of oil supplies. They are feeding into each other. They're creating a double crisis or an aggravated crisis,” he said.“When it comes to food, we are looking at a situation today where some of the major grain exporters will not be able to send out their shipments... We are looking at significant fertilizer shortages... On top of it, we are looking at Super El Niño. There is going to be a major food crisis, probably in the coming months...” he added.Jaishankar said the world was moving “quite visibly” towards greater multipolarity and outlined what he described as a broader approach India could pursue in such an environment.He said countries that were seen as stable, consistent and reliable could become important partners as the global order becomes more competitive.“One, you build a reputation for yourself as stable, consistent, reliable, so that others view you in a very dynamic, volatile world as a steadying factor... Partners tend to gravitate towards you. You're the good person in the neighborhood. The second would be that the more you diversify and you find common interests, common ground, I think the more of a balancing structure can be created. What we have to do is to take self-interest and temper it with a certain long-term, I would say, predictability and stability, which is also part of intelligent self-interest, and try to create something along those lines. ..”He said countries, particularly major trading economies, would seek stability rather than prolonged volatility saying, “...not everybody wants the Hobbesian scenario that you painted; it is very volatile. It's actually very risky in real life. People will not expose their trade accounts to that kind of volatility. For the big trading countries, their economies are exposed to that. Everybody will want to find some accounts of stability... I think the world will go for that kind of mix... The world is more competitive. It's tough. A new dynamic will come.""A new culture will come. New negotiations and new bargains will be struck. When the smoke clears at some point in time, you will see the different points joined by lines of different lengths. There will be a new geometry that will come about. I would still count on the self-interest of countries, their sensibilities and their desire ultimately to stabilize their own lives as a driving force. I think that is the direction we are heading. And we can see that in some of our relationships," he added.
Article Summary: Jaishankar said the two sides had reached “more or less an understanding” on the trade agreement. He said the talks were complex because of the fundamental differences between the two economies. Jaishankar says india-china relations are better than they were in 2025.

Article Title: Kanpur plane crash: No distress call, flight-monitoring gaps emerge in AAIB probe
Article Text:
A four-seater, dual-engine Tecnam aircraft crashed in a fatal crash on the outskirts of the Natthapurwa village near the Ganga Barrage in Kanpur.

No records of flight-data checks

Aircraft stopped responding after final radio call

Engines and flight data being examined

NEW DELHI: The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has found that Garg Aviation did not fully follow required flight-monitoring procedures before its training aircraft crashed near Kanpur on August 27, killing an instructor and a trainee pilot.The seven-page preliminary report also recommends that the Directorate General of Civil Aviation issue clearer guidelines on how Flying Training Organisations should monitor flight data.The Tecnam P2006T twin-engine aircraft crashed near the Ganga Barrage less than 20 minutes after taking off from Kanpur's civil aerodrome. The 39-year-old instructor and 28-year-old trainee were killed.AAIB said Garg Aviation told investigators that it carried out random checks of data from the aircraft's Garmin system. However, the operator could not provide records of those checks and did not have a Standard Operating Procedure explaining how the monitoring was conducted or what limits would trigger further action."When queried on flight data monitoring, the FTO stated that random monitoring of Garmin data was being carried out; however, no records of such monitoring were maintained, and there was no SOP defining how the monitoring was conducted or what exceedance limits were considered for it," AAIB said.The Garmin data card acts as a type of flight-data recorder for small aircraft. AAIB said interim safety recommendations were necessary and called for stricter compliance with flight-data monitoring requirements."Further, DGCA may issue specific guidelines detailing the procedure to be followed for flight data monitoring, which shall be made part of the TPM," the probe agency said. TPM refers to the Training and Procedure Manual.The aircraft, registered as VT-NBV, took off at around 11.11 am on August 27. About 14 minutes later, it made a radio call saying operations were normal and that it would contact the controller again after 10 minutes.That call never came."No further call was received from VT-NBV thereafter. The RT controller attempted to contact VT-NBV but received no response," AAIB said.The aircraft had no distress call before the crash. Garg Aviation was informed at around 12.10 pm that the plane had force-landed in the Ganga Barrage area, after which the company's team went to the site.AAIB said local residents had reported the crash through the 112 emergency helpline. Police and ambulance teams reached the site and took both occupants to a hospital in Kanpur, where they were declared dead.Investigators have recovered the Garmin data card from the wreckage and downloaded its information for analysis. Both engines have also been recovered and quarantined for detailed examination."Both engines have been retrieved and quarantined for further detailed examination. The investigation team is coordinating with the OEM for further examination," it said. OEM refers to Original Equipment Manufacturer.The investigation also involves Italy's ANSV and the US National Transportation Safety Board, which have each appointed an accredited representative. Tecnam has also provided a technical adviser.AAIB has sought documents relating to the aircraft and its operating crew from the DGCA as the investigation continues.The crash occurred at Kanpur's civil aerodrome, an uncontrolled aerodrome managed and maintained by the Airports Authority of India. An uncontrolled aerodrome does not have an operating control tower.
Article Summary: Aircraft stopped responding after final radio call. No records of flight-data checks were maintained. Both engines have been recovered and quarantined for detailed examination. The tecnam p2006t twin-engine aircraft crashed near the ganga barrage less than 20 minutes after taking off.

Article Title: 'Full disclosure of electoral roll changes': Congress's 5 demands amid EC SIR row
Article Text:
Congress attacks EC over SIR row, says will fight ‘to save’ voters’ rights (Image source: X)

Kharge backs Rahul Gandhi’s voter-roll allegations

Congress lists five demands

Full data on major changes to voter lists should be made public.

Voters whose names have been removed should receive complete information and a full opportunity to appeal.

Political parties should receive voter lists and essential related data in a simple format and in a timely manner.

Serious discrepancies should be independently investigated within a fixed timeframe.

Election-related data and decisions should be transparent so that no political party can claim information is being withheld.

“The most important thing is that India's voters must have the confidence that their vote is secure,” Kharge said.

Kharge targets PM Modi, Shah and Election Commission

NEW DELHI: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Tuesday accused the Election Commission of compromising the integrity of the electoral process through the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter rolls and changes to voter-enrolment rules. He also stated that the party would step up its campaign against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the government.Addressing the Congress Working Committee (CWC) meeting, Kharge said the party faced a “historic responsibility” to protect democracy and the Constitution, drawing a parallel between the Congress’ fight for voting rights during British rule and its current campaign over voter rolls.He alleged that names were being removed from electoral rolls “at the behest of the BJP and the Modi government” and accused the CEC of becoming a “puppet” of the government.On the contrary the Election Commission has maintained that its decisions have full legal sanction and that differing views among commissioners are part of institutional deliberations.Kharge also targeted changes to Form 6, which is used for enrolling new voters.He alleged that the rules had been changed in a way that could disenfranchise young voters. He also contrasted Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government with the decision of the Rajiv Gandhi government in 1988 to lower the voting age from 21 to 18.“They didn't provide jobs, and now they don't even want to give the right to vote,” Kharge said, alleging that the government feared questions from the youth.Also read: ‘All SIR rollout decisions unanimous’: EC says agendas for all meetings to be circulated in advance Kharge congratulated Rahul Gandhi for raising questions over voter rolls in Mahadevpuram, Aland and constituencies in Haryana and Maharashtra.He referred to allegations involving duplicate voters, doubtful addresses, multiple voters registered at the same address and entries linked to Form 6, saying the Election Commission should have acted on the issues.“If the Election Commission had shown even a little seriousness in that direction, they would not be in the dock today, and their credibility would have been preserved,” he said.Kharge also praised Congress workers who organised protests at the block, district and state levels following Rahul's campaign.The Congress has been pressing for Kumar's resignation amid a controversy over reported differences within the Election Commission over the SIR exercise. The poll panel has said that operational queries raised by Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi were part of normal institutional deliberations and that its orders followed established procedures.Kharge also questioned the decision-making process behind SIR, asking whether it was wrong to seek clarity on who approved the exercise and why the two election commissioners were allegedly kept out of the internal portal.Kharge laid out five demands that he said the Congress would pursue:He said the Congress did not view the issue merely as a contest over winning or losing elections, arguing that governments may change but democracy and the Constitution were permanent.Kharge also accused the BJP and RSS of systematically weakening independent institutions and said the Congress wanted the Election Commission to be strong enough to command the trust of both the ruling party and opposition.He alleged that two election commissioners had themselves described the CEC's actions as arbitrary and unfair and said those responsible should be removed.Kharge also demanded Prime Minister Narendra Modi's resignation “on moral grounds”, alleging that the CEC had acted under his pressure.The Congress president compared the current controversy with demonetisation, calling the alleged removal of voters from electoral rolls “vote demonetisation”.“In demonetisation, the poor stood in line. In vote demonetisation, the poor has been thrown out of the line altogether,” he said, arguing that voting was the biggest political tool available to poor, Dalit and marginalised citizens.The CWC meeting comes ahead of a meeting of opposition INDIA bloc parties on Wednesday, where a joint strategy on the SIR controversy and the demand for Kumar's removal is expected to be discussed. The opposition is also considering another removal notice against the CEC in Parliament.
Article Summary: Congress attacks ec over sir row, says will fight ‘to save’ voters’ rights.kharge backs rahul gandhi’s voter-roll allegations.congress lists five demands for the election commission. Voters whose names have been removed should receive complete information and a full opportunity to appeal.

The Supreme Court on Tuesday agreed to an early listing of a plea challenging the manner in which the Election Commission of India (ECI) is functioning, with allegations that powers vested in the multi-member constitutional body are being exercised without adhering to the legally mandated collective decision-making process.Senior advocate Vikas Singh mentioned the matter before a bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, arguing that the statutory framework requires decisions of the multi-member Commission to be taken unanimously or by majority.The plea comes amid controversy over ECINet, the ECI’s integrated digital platform for electoral processes. Article Title: Jails are hiring grounds for pro-Khalistan groups; dead drops of ISI modules also under intel lens
Article Text:
Khalistan groups target north India jails to recruit operatives, agencies flag growing threat

NEW DELHI: Intelligence agencies have flagged attempts by pro-Khalistan groups, including Sikhs for Justice (SFJ), to infiltrate jails in north India and recruit operatives. The move comes amid revelations made by a recently detained operative who disclosed having been inducted and given Gurpatwant Singh Pannun's contact while serving time in Patiala jail.Agencies are now investigating the digital footprint, dead-drop financial channels, and the broader jail recruitment network, sources said. Agencies have also noted how ISI-backed modules are increasingly relying on dead-drop methods to channel funds, supply weapons, and execute covert tasks and have largely replaced physical handovers with pre-designated drop points along isolated highway stretches and border and rural sectors.Drawn straight from the classic spycraft playbook, this method ensures that foreign masterminds or handlers remain completely insulated from the foot soldiers executing their commands on the ground. Arms, ammunition, and untraceable cash, frequently delivered across the border via drones or covert couriers, are hidden at specific coordinates, with retrieval instructions transmitted to local operatives over end-to-end encrypted messaging platforms like Signal.The tactic of leveraging prison networks draws from a pattern highlighted by high-profile incidents like the 2016 Nabha jailbreak, which exposed the nexus between terror outfits and incarcerated criminal groups. Within these facilities, handlers and radicalised inmates target vulnerable, economically distressed prisoners - frequently first-time offenders or petty criminals lacking legal representation and financial support.In the latest instance, agencies recently busted an SFJ-backed module and arrested operative Preetpal Singh, who, along with his associates, had spray-painted anti-Brics and pro-Khalistan graffiti across Delhi and Punjab, filmed the act and sent the video to Pannun. Singh, it turned out, had a prior history of pro-Khalistan activities, having been arrested in 2023 for a similar crime.While in prison, he was provided with a phone number to contact Pannun and execute future tasks. After his release in 2026, Singh established direct contact with Pannun and received Rs 1.5 lakh through a dead-drop location on the Faridkot-Amritsar highway. Preetpal subsequently recruited another inmate, also on bail, for the Delhi assignment.
Article Summary: Khalistan groups target north india jails to recruit operatives, agencies flag growing threat. Move comes amid revelations made by a recently detained operative who disclosed having been inducted and given gurpatwant singh pannun's contact while serving time in patiala jail.

Article Text:

NEW DELHI: H1N1 is the dominant flu strain detected in India, accounting for three out of every four influenza-positive samples reported in the latest surveillance data, according to World Health Organization (WHO).The finding is from WHO's surveillance data for weeks 36 and 37 of 2026, covering Sept 1 to 14 and updated on Sept 21. Across the South-East Asia region, 817 of 3,632 samples tested positive for influenza, giving an overall positivity rate of 22%.India stood out for a high share of H1N1 among its positive samples. The A(H1N1)pdm09 accounted for 75% of influenza-positive samples in India, compared with 50% across the region. It was also the dominant strain in Bhutan and Thailand, where it accounted for 97% and74% respectively.Dr Rommel Tickoo, senior director, internal medicine, Max hospital, said H1N1 remains a seasonal strain, with higher complication risks for older adults, pregnant women, young children and people with underlying illnesses. He advised vaccination, respiratory hygiene, early testing where appropriate and timely antiviral treatment for high-risk patients.

Article Title: FBI puts gangster Goldy Brar on Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list
Article Text:
Goldy Brar enters FBI’s Ten Most Wanted list as manhunt goes global

NEW DELHI: Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) has officially placed notorious gangster Satinderjeet Singh aka Goldy Brar, on its famed Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list, offering a reward of up to $1 million for information leading to his arrest.The announcement, made early Tuesday, by the FBI’s Los Angeles Field Office, marks a major escalation in international law enforcement efforts targeting transnational crime syndicates operating across North America and Asia.Brar, who becomes the 543rd fugitive added to the historic list, faces multiple federal indictments in the United States, including Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations (RICO) conspiracy, extortion, and narcotics trafficking.According to federal prosecutors, the fugitive serves as the primary North American operational leader for the Lawrence Bishnoi Organized Crime Group. Operating from a prison cell in India via contraband communications, Bishnoi allegedly delegated international operations to trusted lieutenants like Brar.The syndicate has been linked to a trail of violence across North America, including targeted assassinations, kidnappings, armed extortions, and large-scale drug smuggling—including the theft of over 500 kilograms of cocaine from rival cartels in the Los Angeles region.Among the most high-profile offenses detailed in federal court documents is the June 2023 assassination of prominent political and religious figure "H.S.N." outside a Sikh temple in Surrey, British Columbia.Bishnoi and Brar are charged with ordering the targeted killing. Canadian authorities subsequently designated the Bishnoi syndicate as a terrorist entity in September 2025, highlighting its routine use of public violence and social media threat campaigns to extort individuals within Indian diaspora communities worldwide.Brar’s inclusion on the Top Ten list stems from "Operation Hardball," a years-long multi-agency investigation that unsealed indictments against 37 defendants connected to India-based transnational crime groups in July 2026. While 28 defendants have been taken into custody or located, five key fugitives remain at large alongside Brar.Law enforcement leaders from the FBI, the Los Angeles Police Department, and the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) emphasized that placing Brar on the global list ensures his face will be publicized worldwide until he is captured.Considered armed, extremely violent, and dangerous, Brar is believed to be hiding in parts of California or Canada. Authorities advise the public to avoid direct interaction and to submit tips directly to the FBI.
Article Summary: Goldy brar is the 543rd fugitive added to the fbi's ten most wanted fugitives list. Brar faces multiple federal indictments in the united states, including racketeer influenced and corrupt organizations (rico) conspiracy, extortion, and narcotics trafficking.

Article Title: Indian imports of Russian crude oil to decline further amid lower exports, Chinese competition
Article Text:
Tourists watch marine life, with the MT Desert Kite oil tanker carrying Russian oil in the background (Photo: Reuters).

NEW DELHI: Indian refiners expect Russian oil supplies to decline further in October and November, owing to lower exports and stiff competition from China, forcing the country to buy costlier alternatives for the rest of the year.People familiar with procurement plans told Reuters that some Indian refiners would not receive adequate Russian supplies in October and November."Demand from China has been really high. They were willing to book cargoes in advance and to pay firmer prices compared to Indian refiners," a source involved in the sale of Russian crude said.According to analytics firm Kpler, Russian oil arrivals in India are set to drop to around 1.75 million barrels per day in September, the lowest level since April.Trade data showed that arrivals had already fallen 16.5 per cent to about 2.1 million bpd in August from July, although Russia remained India's main supplier, ahead of the UAE and Venezuela.Overall availability of Russian exports has reportedly shrunk, particularly from the Black Sea port of Novorossiysk, where shipments have roughly halved as repeated drone attacks have suspended loadings.India has been the top buyer of seaborne Russian Urals crude since 2022, when Moscow diverted its energy flows away from Europe at deep discounts.In recent months, however, China, the world's top crude importer, has stepped up its purchases as Middle Eastern supplies tightened because of the Iran war.Traders told Reuters that refiners have turned to pricier replacement barrels, seeking UAE Murban, a close substitute for Russia's Urals grade, while also buying Iraqi Basrah and Angolan cargoes.Shipping dynamics have helped redirect flows to China.Seasonal navigation along the Arctic Northern Sea Route (NSR) offers a secure and cost-effective channel for Russian crude exports to China, whereas shipments to India via the Red Sea face heightened security risks linked to the conflict involving Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis."It's not so much about the price as ensuring the cargo actually reaches its destination," another trader told Reuters, adding that freight costs via the Arctic route to China are now broadly comparable with shipments through the Suez Canal.
Article Summary: India has been the top buyer of seaborne russian urals crude since 2022. China, the world's top crude importer, has stepped up its purchases as middle eastern supplies tightened because of the iran war. Indian refiners have turned to pricier replacement barrels, seeking uae murban, a close substitute for russia's urals grade.

Article Title: ‘Beating his drum away’: Congress targets PM Modi for ‘ignoring’ rising inflation in Mann Ki Baat
Article Text:
Cong targets PM Modi for 'ignoring' inflation

(With ANI inputs)

NEW DELHI: The Congress on Monday questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi for not addressing rising inflation in his Mann Ki Baat radio address, accusing him of being “blissfully unconcerned” about the issue.The opposition party’s attack came a day after PM Modi addressed the nation in the 138th episode of Mann Ki Baat.“The brunt of inflation is no longer confined just to the kitchen, yet the Prime Minister remains blissfully unconcerned, beating his drum away. Vegetables are getting more expensive by the day, with onion prices soaring 48.27% in August. Items such as air conditioners, TVs and refrigerators are also set to become more expensive. Household savings are steadily declining, while family debt is mounting. In such a scenario, how is the common family supposed to meet its needs?” Congress MP Jairam Ramesh wrote on X.Ramesh questioned why PM Modi continues to “sermonise” in the Mann Ki Baat series instead of addressing the public’s concerns.“In his ‘Mann Ki Baat’ radio series, the Prime Minister keeps sermonising on various issues, but when will he address the country’s most pressing concern—inflation? When will he care about the public’s worries? The public is already beleaguered by rising prices, and there’s no relief coming from the government.How on earth is the average family supposed to manage its budget? How long will the middle class and the poor have their backs broken like this?” the Rajya Sabha MP asked.According to the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation’s (MoSPI) Consumer Price Index (CPI) release, retail inflation, based on the 2024=100 CPI, stood at 4.82% in August, up from 4.45% in July. Food inflation, measured by the Consumer Food Price Index (CFPI), rose to 5.95% in August from 5.52% in July. The August figures are provisional.Official data showed that onion inflation surged from 22.54% in July to 48.27% in August. Ginger recorded inflation of 73.82%, while garlic inflation stood at 43.60%. In contrast, tomato prices fell 31.09% year-on-year, while potato prices declined 13.14%.MoSPI data showed inflation in the combined food and beverages category at 5.66% in August. Transport inflation stood at 4.60 percent, education services at 3.73%, while restaurants and accommodation services recorded inflation of 8.38%. Personal care, social protection and miscellaneous goods and services registered inflation of 15.17%.The CPI data was compiled from price information collected across 1,407 urban markets, including online markets, and 1,465 villages nationwide. MoSPI reported a 100% response rate from both rural and urban markets in August.According to MoSPI, the next CPI data, covering September, is scheduled to be released on October 12.

Article Title: India's Essar Group to invest $15 billion in 'largest' US steel plant, Trump announces
Article Text:
President Donald Trump speaks as from right, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, Energy Secretary Chris Wright, Essar Capital Director Prashant Ruia, Mesabi Metallics Chairman Rewant Ruia and Mesabi Metallics CEO Joe Broking

Project to link

Minnesota iron ore mine

with

Iowa steel plant

US President Donald Trump on Tuesday announced plans by Indian conglomerate Essar Group, through its US subsidiary Mesabi Metallics, to invest about $15 billion in a major steel plant in Iowa.Trump made the announcement at the White House alongside Essar Group co-founder Ravi Ruia and Mesabi Metallics chairman Rewant Ruia, describing the project as the largest steel plant in American history."Today we're thrilled to announce that Mesabi Metallics will be building the largest steel plant in American history in the great state of Iowa. It's the largest plant, one of the largest plants in the world, but it's the largest plant in America by far," Trump told reporters.The facility is expected to produce 10 million tonnes of steel a year once fully operational, with production targeted to begin in 2030. The project is also expected to create thousands of jobs during construction and nearly 2,000 permanent positions across the steel and mining operations.The Iowa plant will form part of an integrated US supply chain, with iron ore sourced from a new mine being developed by Mesabi Metallics in Minnesota's Mesabi Iron Range.The company has invested about $2.5 billion in the mine, which is expected to produce around 7.5 million tonnes of iron annually and create about 350 jobs.Rewant Ruia said he was born in India but had studied in New York, Boston and California, adding that he had spent half his life in the US and described the investment as "a true homecoming". He said the project would establish a fully integrated supply chain "from mine to mill".Trump highlighted the domestic nature of the operation, saying the Minnesota mine would be "the first new iron ore mine in the United States in more than 50 years with the highest quality ore.""In other words, this steel will be mined, melted, and made right here in the USA, which is something very unusual," Trump said.Rewant Ruia thanked the president "for bringing back the importance of building things in America." He also said the plant would use advanced technology and "will compete head-to-head with any steel plant in the world on size, quality and on cost."Trump and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick attributed the investment partly to the administration's steel tariffs. Trump said companies were building in the US "because they don't want to pay tariffs".
Article Summary: Indian conglomerate essar group to invest about $15 billion in a major steel plant in iowa. The facility is expected to produce 10 million tonnes of steel a year once fully operational, with production targeted to begin in 2030. The project is also expected to create thousands of jobs during construction and nearly 2,000 permanent positions across the steel and mining operations.

Article Title: Father left $21 million in a charitable fund; son sought a $1 million donation but his access was cut off by the foundation
Article Text:
Philip Peterson, left, with his father Gordon in 2015. Image Credit: CNBC

How did the $21 million fund become the subject of a lawsuit

What changed between Peterson and WaterStone

WaterStone is based in northeast Colorado Springs. Image Credit: The Gazette

$1 million donation at the centre of the dispute

What does the lawsuit say about control of donor-advised funds

The case could clarify duties and rights of successor advisers and sponsors

A $21 million charitable fund is at the centre of a legal dispute after Philip Peterson, the son of its founder, alleged that WaterStone cut off his access and stopped acting on his recommendations. The fund was created by Gordon Peterson in 2005 for Christian charitable causes, and Philip became its sole successor adviser after his mother died. According to the lawsuit, the dispute escalated in 2024, when access to the account was revoked and a proposed $1 million donation was not processed. The case is now examining how much authority successor advisers actually have over donor-advised funds.Gordon Peterson established the Peterson Family Stewardship Fund with WaterStone in 2005. The fund was intended to support evangelical Christian charitable purposes. WaterStone, the name used by Christian Community Foundation, became responsible for holding and administering the money.According to MinistryWatch , Gordon died in 2019. His wife Ruth and son Philip had been recognised as advisers to the family fund from 2017. When Ruth died in 2021, Philip became the sole successor adviser. For several years, WaterStone continued to process the charitable grants he recommended.The fund was worth more than $21 million by the end of 2023, according to the lawsuit. CNBC reported that Peterson had continued to make recommendations from the account until the relationship with WaterStone deteriorated in 2024. At that point, he says, his access to information about the fund was cut off.The disagreement appears to have centred on how the fund would be managed and distributed in the future. CNBC reported that Peterson disagreed with WaterStone over a proposal concerning the fund's principal and investment income. He subsequently raised the possibility of moving the fund to another sponsor.According to MinistryWatch, Peterson says a March 5, 2024 Zoom call with WaterStone chief executive Ken Harrison ended with Peterson being told that further communication with the organisation would cease. Peterson then tried to restore access and contacted board members, but says those efforts did not resolve the dispute.The lawsuit alleges that WaterStone revoked his online access, suspended his advisory privileges and stopped processing his grant recommendations. Foley & Lardner reported that Peterson also alleges WaterStone refused to provide information about the account and directed him to stop contacting the organisation.One of the most significant recommendations involved a proposed $1 million grant to Operation Mobilization, a Christian missionary organisation that had previously received support from the Peterson family fund.MinistryWatch reported that Peterson says WaterStone denied the distribution after previously approving and administering his recommendations. It also reported that the fund made no charitable grants in 2024, according to the lawsuit.The issue was particularly important to Peterson because Operation Mobilization had a history of receiving support from his family. His lawsuit argues that WaterStone's actions interfered with the charitable purpose for which his father had established the fund.In February 2025, WaterStone agreed to make $400,000 in distributions, according to MinistryWatch. Peterson accepted those distributions but also raised concerns that the fund was still behind on charitable contributions from earlier years.The case raises a broader issue because a donor-advised fund does not work like a personal bank account for charitable giving. Once money is contributed, the sponsoring organisation legally controls the assets, while the donor or successor adviser can recommend where grants should go.Foley & Lardner explained that this distinction is central to this case. The law firm said WaterStone's sponsorship agreement gives it ultimate control and discretion over the fund and states that the original donor irrevocably gave up ownership and other rights to the contributions. That arrangement is common to donor-advised funds. The adviser can have an important role in suggesting charitable grants, but the sponsor retains legal control over the money.Peterson's lawsuit seeks more than the payment of one disputed grant. According to MinistryWatch, he is asking for an accounting of the fund, clarification of the rights and duties between himself and WaterStone, and an order requiring the organisation to carry out its responsibilities, including recommended grants. He is also seeking to transfer the fund to another organisation.Foley & Lardner reports that the case could clarify whether advisory rights that donors and successor advisers commonly rely upon are legally enforceable. WaterStone has argued in its motion to dismiss that it is not contractually required to follow Peterson's recommendations because the sponsorship agreement leaves ultimate authority with WaterStone.The case reaches beyond the Peterson family. It could help clarify what happens when a donor-advised fund sponsor and a successor adviser no longer agree about how charitable money should be handled.
Article Summary: Philip peterson, the son of the fund's founder, alleges waterstone cut off his access and stopped acting on his recommendations. The dispute escalated in 2024, when access to the account was revoked and a proposed $1 million donation was not processed. The case is now examining how much authority successor advisers have over donor-advised funds.

Article Title: 8 US Marines hurt in previously unreported Iranian strikes; possible traumatic brain injuries: Report
Article Text:
File photo: Vessel attacked in Strait of Hormuz

Marines were not aboard US Navy ship

Pentagon casualty figures under scrutiny

Eight US Marines were injured in a previously undisclosed attack in the Strait of Hormuz on September 14, NBC News reported, citing three US officials.The Marines were part of a battalion landing team when the missile hit the vessel, the officials said. Seven were enlisted personnel and one was an officer. None suffered serious injuries, but they experienced smoke inhalation and concussion-like symptoms, including headaches, with officials saying some may have sustained traumatic brain injuries.All eight returned to duty shortly after the attack, according to the officials.The vessel struck in the attack was not a US Navy ship, according to the officials, who did not identify its type and referred to it only as a maritime vessel.The Pentagon did not publicly report the September 14 attack or the injuries at the time. The eight Marines were added to the Defense Casualty Analysis System nearly 10 days after the incident.One US official attributed the delay partly to injuries such as concussion symptoms that can take time to emerge, as well as the casualty database not being updated in real time.As of Wednesday, the Pentagon database had recorded 861 US service members as injured in the war with Iran, with the eight Marines included in that tally.The disclosure comes as the Pentagon faces renewed scrutiny over how it reports US military casualties in the conflict.A Washington Post report said at least four US service members killed in the Middle East since the war began were not reflected in the official casualty count at the time. The Pentagon has also faced accusations of downplaying some injuries reported by wounded troops.The US military has disputed those allegations, saying casualty classifications such as “not seriously injured” and “combat casualty” have specific definitions that can be misunderstood.The newly reported Marine injuries add another previously undisclosed incident to the broader debate over how quickly US military casualties are recorded and publicly reported during the conflict.
Article Summary: Marines were part of a battalion landing team when the missile hit the vessel, officials said. None suffered serious injuries, but they experienced smoke inhalation and concussion-like symptoms, including headaches. Pentagon did not publicly report the september 14 attack or the injuries at the time.

Article Title: Who was behind RAF Fairford terror plot? 'Foreign actor' claim puts Iran link in focus
Article Text:
File photo: United States Air Force personnel at RAF Fairford

Trump says plot ‘might’ be linked to Iran

What happened near RAF Fairford?

The suspected terror plot near RAF Fairford has put a possible Iran link back in focus after US secretary of state Marco Rubio said a foreign actor was “clearly” involved, without naming the country or providing evidence. The development comes as British counter-terrorism investigators continue to examine whether the five men arrested near the airbase had links to a foreign state.Rubio made the claim after five British men arrested near the US-used airbase were released on police bail and stated that the incident “clearly involves the hands of a foreign actor”.The men, all British nationals in their early 20s from London, remain under investigation and have been placed under stringent conditions governing their movement and contact with others. UK counter-terrorism police have said their release does not mean the investigation is over.US president Donald Trump also weighed in on Monday, saying he would not have released the suspects on bail.Asked whether the case was linked to Iran, Trump said: “It might.” He declined to elaborate, saying he knew the answer but preferred not to disclose it.Trump had earlier said the suspects wanted to cause “big damage” and suggested they had been under investigation by British and US authorities.British sources, however, have indicated that while the broader threat environment was known, the specific activities of the five men were not necessarily known.Iran, however, has strongly denied any involvement in the incident. The Iranian embassy in London “categorically rejects and strongly condemns” what it called “unfounded and malicious speculations” by British individuals and media outlets attempting to link Tehran to the arrest of the five suspects near RAF Fairford.The embassy said such claims, particularly following what it described as US and Israeli “criminal acts of aggression” against Iran, would only fuel “Iranophobia propaganda” in the UK. It also said Iran reserved the right to take legal measures to protect the country’s rights and interests in response to what it called misleading and damaging media narratives.Police were alerted early Sunday after a local farmer reported seeing three white vans and a group of hooded or masked men near the base.Armed officers arrested five men in the Whelford area, about a mile from RAF Fairford. They were initially held on suspicion of offences under the Explosives Act and were later arrested on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act. Around 85 homes were evacuated and a 400-metre cordon was imposed while bomb-disposal teams and forensic experts examined the vehicles.An initial examination of the vans led investigators to assess whether they contained explosive materials. British media later reported that no viable explosives had been found.The head of UK Counter Terrorism Policing, assistant commissioner Laurence Taylor, said investigators were considering “multiple lines of enquiry”, including the possibility that the activity involved proxies or individuals knowingly or unknowingly working for a foreign state.The possibility of an Iranian connection has drawn particular attention because RAF Fairford has been used by US bombers in operations against Iran.Iran's Revolutionary Guards had previously warned that the base could be considered a legitimate target if it was used to launch attacks. The area has also seen increased security activity amid tensions between Britain, the US and Iran.British defence secretary Wes Streeting said Iran and its proxies were known to pose threats, while foreign secretary Ed Miliband said Britain had to be prepared to confront security threats and Iranian proxies.But neither British counter-terrorism police nor the government has publicly established that Iran was behind the Fairford incident.The investigation therefore remains open to several possibilities, with police examining whether the suspects acted independently, on behalf of a foreign state or as proxies.
Article Summary: Us secretary of state marco rubio said a foreign actor was ‘clearly’ involved, without naming the country or providing evidence. The development comes as british counter-terrorism investigators continue to examine whether the five men arrested near the airbase had links to a foreign state.

Article Title: Trump embraces Xi as peer, alarms partners and critics
Article Text: TOI correspondent from Washington: A 48-hour state visit to the United States by China’s President Xi Jinping yielded no immediate major breakthroughs but confirmed the broad impression, in visuals and much as words, that Washington now accepts China as a peer in a new G-2 formulation.For all the talk of trade, artificial intelligence, Taiwan, Iran and strategic competition, the most consequential message of Xi’s visit may have been the choreography itself. A fawning Trump repeatedly described Xi as a friend and the relationship as a “great friendship,” with little personal reciprocity from the Chinese leader.The charitable explanation for what many critics said was Trump’s folding before Xi and muting his demands from and tirades against China was purportedly in the service of American farmers – his major voting bloc – who are getting screwed because Beijing cut down purchase of soy, corn, and other farm produce. In brief remarks during a tea ceremony, the MAGA supremo mentioned that the visit had yielded “great results” for American farmers without elaborating, but spoke of little else other than accepting Xi’s invitation to visit China.By most accounts, the summit produced a lot of optics, but little else, amid a cascade of criticism that Trump is placating China rather than confronting it over its actions inimical to US, including its tacit support for Iran.The most withering censure came from Republican Senator John Kennedy of Louisiana, who likened Xi and leaders of Russia, North Korea and Iran, to reptiles. "The chief reptile, the quarterback, is President Xi. They all lie like timeshare salesmen. You can’t trust them. I wouldn’t turn my back on any of them, even if I thought and knew they were two days dead,” Kennedy told a TV show during the visit. Even Senator Chuck Grassley, the Iowa Republican whose state is deeply dependent on agricultural exports, was sceptical about the outcome of the visit, saying that if extending the trade truce was all that emerged, the summit risked becoming a “show job" for a communist autocrat.On Taiwan, the most sensitive strategic issue between the two sides, there was no public breakthrough. Trump has continued to hold in abeyance a roughly $14 billion Taiwan weapons package that he described earlier this year as a negotiating chip with Beijing. China wants the arms sales halted; US lawmakers across party lines have urged their release.Nor were there any signs of a significant Chinese concession on Iran. Beijing has expressed interest in peace and stability but remains economically intertwined with Tehran. On advanced chips, Washington also appeared to hold its line, despite Beijing’s interest in easing US technology restrictions. That may ultimately prove more consequential than the ceremonial theatrics. The summit thus produced no obvious quid pro quo in which China would use its leverage over Iran in return for a major American concession.Trump’s defenders argued though that the president’s approach should be judged against what they described as decades of failed China policy under previous administrations. “Obama and Biden talked tough, but gave away American factories to the Chinese. Trump actually launched a trade war against China,” noted Brian Kilmeade on Fox News, pointing out that Trump "kicked the Chinese out of Panama Canal" and went after their “favourite oil proxies in our hemisphere, Venezuela and Iran, and is about to kick them out of Cuba. ”That in essence is the larger contradiction of the summit. Trump has not abandoned confrontation with China; he has instead recast it as transactional management between two superpowers, much to the consternation of other nations like India, Japan, and South Korea. Xi, for his part, repeatedly spoke not of friendship between two men but of China and the US as “two major countries” with a responsibility to find a new way of coexisting.The symbolism was perhaps captured most neatly by the contrasting tours offered during the two leaders’ encounters. When Trump visited Beijing in May, Xi showed him ancient trees at Zhongnanhai, including specimens more than 1,000 years old — a quiet display of Chinese historical depth and long-term continuity. In Washington, Trump showed Xi his new White House helipad, built in a “record” 12 weeks – which the Chinese would have built in 12 days if not 12 hours.
Article Summary: Xi jinping's 48-hour state visit to the united states yielded no immediate major breakthroughs. But it confirmed the broad impression, in visuals and much as words, that washington now accepts china as a peer in a new g-2 formulation.

Article Title: ‘No Muslim can even dare’: Pakistan PM at UN condemns Houthi attacks, draws red line over Mecca
Article Text:
Pakistan's PM Shehbaz Sharif speaks at UNGA

NEW DELHI: Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday used the 81st United Nations General Assembly to condemn Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and warn against any threat to the safety and sanctity of Mecca.He also defended Pakistan’s new defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Türkiye, while highlighting Islamabad’s diplomatic efforts to bring the United States and Iran to the negotiating table."We once again condemn, in the strongest possible terms, the recent deplorable attacks by the Houthis against the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia," Sharif said in his address."The attempted drone attack on the holy city of Mecca al-Mukarramah has outraged Muslims across the globe. Any threat to safety and sanctity... is a red line that must never be crossed. No Muslim can even dare to think of committing such a heinous (act)."Saudi Arabia has accused the Houthis of targeting Mecca with a drone, an allegation the Houthis denied. Riyadh has also reported intercepting Houthi ballistic missiles following renewed hostilities in the region.Sharif also sought to underline Islamabad’s diplomatic role in the conflict between the United States and Iran, saying Pakistan had worked to bring the two sides to the negotiating table.“Pakistan chose to act swiftly through concerted efforts. Pakistan successfully brought Washington and Tehran under one roof in Islamabad. From the Islamabad talks to the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding, many historic steps were taken to bring an end to this serious conflict,” he said.The Pakistani prime minister also referred to the recently signed defence agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye. The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement provides for collective defence commitments among the three countries, while Pakistani officials have said the arrangement is not directed against any particular state.Sharif said the pact was intended to serve defence, stability and peace rather than confrontation.On Palestine, Sharif denounced what he called Israel’s “genocidal agenda” and condemned what he described as “Israeli aggression against Lebanon and Syria”.He also thanked Pakistan’s Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff, Field Marshal Asim Munir, crediting his “relentless efforts” with helping create “space for diplomacy under exceptionally difficult and challenging circumstances”.Sharif further thanked US President Donald Trump for what he called his “timely intervention” during the 2025 India-Pakistan conflict, saying it had “saved hundreds of millions of lives in South Asia”.His remarks came as Pakistan balances its ties with Iran with its deepening strategic and defence relationship with Saudi Arabia, while regional tensions continue to test Islamabad’s stated preference for diplomacy.
Article Summary: Pakistan's pm shehbaz sharif condemns houthi attacks on saudi arabia. Warns against any threat to the safety and sanctity of mecca. Defends pakistan's new defence pact with saudi arabia and türkiye. Underlines islamabad's diplomatic efforts to bring u.s. and iran to negotiating table.

Article Title: $26,000 to fight for Russia: How Moscow recruits Americans via TikTok and Telegram
Article Text:
File photo: Russian President Vladimir Putin arrives for a wreath-laying ceremony surrounded by Russian military personnels

US citizens joining Russia's war

Russia is increasingly turning to foreign recruits to replenish its forces fighting in Ukraine, with at least 18 Americans identified as having joined the Russian military, according to Ukrainian officials cited by the New York Post. US recruits are reportedly being offered a signing bonus of about $26,000, along with a monthly salary.The recruitment is being driven through a network of agents who use platforms including Facebook, TikTok and Telegram to find potential recruits. Ukrainian officials said recruiters can earn money for each person they bring in, with some reportedly receiving about $24,000 per recruit as well as a share of the recruit’s salary.The effort extends far beyond Americans. Ukrainian security officials have identified nearly 29,000 foreigners from 135 countries fighting for Russia, although the actual number could be higher. Amnesty International has separately documented deceptive and exploitative recruitment practices targeting foreign nationals, including promises of civilian jobs, high salaries, legal status or Russian citizenship.One of those recruited was Seth William Baker, a former US Marine from Gilbert, Arizona. Baker, who had served as a lance corporal and worked as a bulk fuel specialist, was 23 when he was killed on the frontlines in Ukraine, around three months after signing up.Baker had joined the Marines at 18 but was later discharged after refusing the military's Covid-19 vaccine mandate. He subsequently became involved with Russian propaganda online before travelling to Russia.In a recording made from a Russian bunker, Baker said the vaccine mandate had been one of the factors behind his decision to leave the US military and join Russia's war effort.Vitaliy Matvienko, who heads Ukraine's state-backed project encouraging Russian soldiers to surrender, described Baker's case as typical of the people Russia's recruitment network seeks out. He said Russia had turned foreign recruitment into an “entire industry” as it struggles to replace battlefield losses.Baker is not the only American identified as having fought for Russia.Michael Gloss, 21, the son of a former CIA official, was killed while fighting in Ukraine in April 2024. Ukrainian intelligence has also identified 17 other Americans who had enlisted in the Russian military.Another case involves former Massachusetts city councillor Wilmer Puello-Mota, who left the US while facing a child sexual-abuse-related case and later joined Russian forces. He was wounded by shrapnel in Ukraine in August.Derek Huffman, 47, moved his family to Russia and later signed up for the military, according to the report. He had previously criticised what he described as LGBTQ “indoctrination” in the US and said he wanted to earn respect and Russian citizenship.Matvienko said foreign recruits serve a dual purpose for Moscow: they provide additional manpower while also allowing Russia to portray Americans and other foreigners fighting alongside its troops as evidence of international support for its war.Foreign recruits can also be easier for Russia to absorb politically when they are killed, he said, because their deaths do not necessarily generate the same reaction inside Russian society as the deaths of Russian soldiers.The recruitment comes as Russia continues to sustain heavy battlefield losses. Ukrainian officials cited by the New York Post estimated that Russia was suffering tens of thousands of casualties each month and increasingly relying on foreign nationals to help fill its ranks.
Article Summary: Us recruits are reportedly being offered a signing bonus of about $26,000. Ukrainian security officials have identified nearly 29,000 foreigners from 135 countries fighting for russia. The recruitment is being driven through a network of agents who use platforms including facebook, tiktok and telegram to find potential recruits.
